abstract.text: Inherited from
The active fold across the screen;
when the display is flat, closed, or has no hinge.
The Mac overview, while it is up.
Whether a swipe down from the top edge, or an iPad pointer at the top, brings the stream’s
buttons back: only while they are put away for the Mac.
Whether What works now is up.
Whether Headwire Helper is told this screen is kept awake over the Mac’s picture, so it
keeps the Mac’s display awake for someone watching without touching anything.
The overview’s newest picture of each Mac it shows, by the Mac’s ID.
The paired Mac on screen: the one the helper link reached, else the one chosen, else the
only one paired. The Mac menu’s checkmark and everything published outside the app read it.
Which of what a waiting intent may need is up: input, then the picture.
Whether the Picture in Picture window is open or opening, while input to the Mac stays off.
Whether a hardware keyboard is connected, which on an iPad leaves the Mac keys off by default.
Where the sound comes from: the video on screen.
Whether a screen that offers pairing with a helper nearby is up: the settings sheet or What
works now, once Pair with your Mac has opened.
Whether some input surface sends to the Mac and the pointer is locked.
Whether this is an iPad or an iPhone, which has no keyboard of its own.
The stream quality asked of the helper, and the level it reports.
Whether locked Pro features show, as Settings > Advanced stores it.
Whether the tip prompt has to wait, for anything else on screen.
A sheet or alert presented over the stream, in the order they take the screen.
The Mac’s sound, from the video on screen.
The buttons over a streaming picture, folded into a chevron or open.
The first-start question about sharing usage data.
Whether the picture can be seen: in the foreground, or in the Picture in Picture window,
opening included (an automatic start says so as it begins), so going into Picture in
Picture never asks the Mac to mirror on the way. Sound alone keeps Headwire running but
shows nothing.
Whether the settings button is drawn dimmed: only while video is up, so it stays easy to find otherwise.
Whether three fingers drag: as the Mac’s own setting, once its helper has reported it, else
as the person set it in Settings.
The banner naming every way to drive the Mac, while nothing can.
How the screen is divided: split at an active fold, with or without video, otherwise spanning.
The stream’s sheets SwiftUI has on screen, as the view reports them: from their content
appearing until their dismissal has finished.
Whether the settings button is fully shown or dimmed after inactivity, with the keyboard button and an auto-hiding key row.
Whether auto-lock is held off: while a picture of the Mac shows, or the trackpad pane is up
to drive it, and the person wants the screen kept awake. A card left on screen while its
Mac sleeps, or the helper’s stream while the Mac’s display sleeps, shows no picture of it,
so the iPad dims and locks as it would without Headwire.
The stream filling the screen.
The session count and the tip prompt.
Whether tap to point and Apple Pencil reach the Mac’s picture: not while the Mac is extended
onto this screen and input goes over Bluetooth, whose absolute pointer can’t aim at that display.
Whether the stream’s buttons may be put away: input reaches the Mac from the stream, which
it never does with a sheet or alert over it. Without input the chevron’s no-input mark stays findable.
What the helper says of each of its features, only while a helper link is up: a Mac name
remembered from an old link is not a link, and every request these features make rides it.
Whether the usage data question has to wait, for anything else on screen.
What the screen shows of the stream’s buttons: open with nothing streaming, so the way to
Settings stays in sight, and dimmed or hidden only while
holds.
Whether what a request needs is up now.
The other paired Macs the glance asks for pictures, over the picture routes that are on but
Direct wireless; none while the overview is open, since its own links carry them then.
The clipboard and files between this device and the Mac.
The Mac on screen as the glance sees it, or
while no paired Mac is connected and shown.
The Mac’s picture in the Dynamic Island and the widgets, in the background.
Whether features only the Direct download has show, as Settings > Advanced stores it.
The screen edges whose first swipe the app takes ahead of the system, each only while the
app has a swipe of its own there.
How touches move the Mac’s pointer.
The helper stream’s size for the upscaling picker, while Settings is up and the stream is on screen.
The video path whose picture of the Mac shows now: on screen, and carrying the Mac’s picture.
The Mac on screen as the Live Activity shows it, or
while no named Mac is connected.
The settings sheet, while it is up.
Screenshots, recordings and Live Text of the Mac’s picture.
The iPad and iPhone app: one screen that shows the Mac’s picture and sends the Mac input from touch, trackpad, mouse, Pencil, and keyboard.
The mirror’s snapshot, published each time it changes and once as the paired list is first
read, even when that is no Macs and so no change: a mirror a backup restored, or one kept
from a list since lost, would otherwise list Macs that aren’t paired until the next pairing.
Whether the keyboard button shows beside the settings button: over video, whenever the key
row, and the keyboard key in it, isn’t showing; and on the trackpad pane with no video,
where there is no key row.
The state a launch starts from: away, until the scene says it came to the foreground.
The paired Macs and the one on screen, as the mirror lists them.
Whether the helper’s stream mirrors the Mac or extends it onto this screen.
Whether this display has shown a fold since launch; iPhone Duo closed looks like any iPhone.
Which Bluetooth host gets input, and the question about a new one.
The question before the helper link pairs over the Bluetooth bond.
Whether the scene is in the foreground, rather than in the background or not yet shown.
Whether the Picture in Picture button shows: on a device that has it, while there is video
to put in the window, and not while the person hides Pro’s locked features.
Whether Headwire keeps running now, so its links stay up: in the foreground, or in the
background with the Mac’s sound playing or Picture in Picture open.
Whether a recording that just finished, or anything else waiting to be captured, has to
wait: for anything else on screen, or for the editor or clip before it still animating away.
The Picture in Picture window.
Whether Pair with your Mac has opened once, before which nothing browses for helpers nearby.
Whether the row of stream buttons is open, which holds off the idle interval’s dimming.
Whether an input path reaches the Mac: Bluetooth connected, or the helper allowed to post input.
What VoiceOver hears about the stream, from the facts the screen draws.
The key row’s keys a finger is holding down, which keep the row on auto-hide from fading.
How the stream gives way to the on-screen keyboard: not at all while it is down; with it
up, by sliding to the top on a screen of compact height, and by fitting above it otherwise.
What the no-input banner decides from.
The notice naming characters Bluetooth couldn’t type.
Whether the on-screen keyboard is up for typing to the Mac.
The recording intent waiting for the recorder to say it started or stopped, by its ticket.
Every presentation that wants the screen or is still on it, in the order they take it.
How the key row is drawn: only over video, and as the person’s setting says.
Every video and input path’s health, and the live pair.
Which surface takes input: the stream’s while video is up, else the trackpad pane’s, never
under any of the screen’s
s, or while the Mac is in a Picture in
Picture window.
Whether the Mac keys strip rides on the on-screen keyboard: while it is up, as the person’s
setting says, which by default is on iPhone and on an iPad with no hardware keyboard.
Records the active fold, or its loss, and places the stream beside the trackpad at one.
Whether
is on screen from
, the stream (
) or the settings sheet:
it wants the screen, only
is before it, and on the stream no other sheet is still
on screen, closing or put away.
How touches move the Mac’s pointer now: as the person chose, or as a trackpad while tap to point can’t reach the picture.
Pro’s entitlement and its sheet.
The intents waiting for input or the picture.
The one screen: the stream, a settings button that dims when idle, the key row, and the settings sheet.
The facts the feature gate reads.
The strip of Mac keys over the on-screen keyboard.
